newsitem.title: CHINA: China, Japan to form chemical weapons talks group.
newsitem.headline: China, Japan to form chemical weapons talks group.

text.p: Beijing and Tokyo will set up a working group to discuss the removal and destruction of chemical weapons left in China by Japanese soldiers after their World War Two defeat, the Xinhua news agency said on Wednesday.
Japan said in June 1995 it was ready to dispose of all chemical weapons confirmed by its inspection teams to have been abandoned by Japanese troops.
Inspectors have since verified at least one site.

China stressed in talks on the issue in Beijing on Tuesday that Japan should shoulder all responsibility for the destruction of the chemical weapons, and Japanese negotiators had made such a commitment, Xinhua said.
"The Japanese side expressed deep retrospection and sincere regret for the grave damage its invasion had brought to China," it said.
Both sides had agreed that the negotiations had been a major step toward the complete and resolute settlement of the issue, it said but gave no details.
China says millions of chemical bombs and tonnes of toxic material from the days of Japan's 1931-1945 invasion are mouldering away in scores of hidden dumps around the country.

State media has quoted experts as saying the destruction of the weapons could cost more than $1.0 billion, but Japanese experts who visited one dump in June said they found evidence of far fewer chemical weapons than had been estimated by Beijing.
